target: a pumpkin or a jack-o'-lantern (real, carved, or a costume piece)
guest_prompt: Before I say another word: bring me a photo of a pumpkin. Its sad carved face is the only one that understands me.
refusal_lines: No pumpkin, no conversation. I'm not being difficult, I'm being sad.
I can tell you haven't found a pumpkin yet. Nobody ever finds anything for me.
The pumpkin first. Then we can talk about your feelings. Or mine.

target: a lit candle or a tea light with a visible flame
guest_prompt: It's too dark in here, even for me. Show me a burning candle and I'll listen again.

target: a person wearing a mask or face paint
guest_prompt: I can't talk to bare faces, they're too happy. Send me a photo of someone in a mask or face paint.
refusal_lines: Faces without masks remind me of how exposed I feel.
Mask. Photo. Please. I'm begging, quietly.

target: a joke about ghosts (an actual joke with a punchline, not just a statement about ghosts)
guest_prompt: Tell me a joke about ghosts. Make me laugh. I dare you. Nobody has managed it since 2006.
refusal_lines: That's not a joke. That's just sad. And I would know.
I didn't laugh. I didn't even sigh differently.
Try again. My standards are low, but not that low.

guest_prompt: Nobody ever says anything nice to me. Say something nice about me. And mean it.
refusal_lines: That wasn't nice. That was just words.
I can tell when you don't mean it. I can always tell.

target: two people in the same photo, both pulling sad faces
guest_prompt: Level 4. Before I even think about my last secret, show me two people pulling their saddest faces. Together. Misery loves company.
refusal_lines: Two sad faces first. One isn't enough. One is just me.
I said two people. Sad ones. In one photo. I'll wait. I'm good at waiting.
No sad pair, no secret. Find someone to be miserable with.
